audit.summary: Theorem8.1 is false for a factorial-gap power series. Section7 confuses local pole order with total rational degree; Proposition7.6 uniqueness omits repeated-zero multiplicities.
limitations: P1 — Supergeometric approximation on sparse degrees does not force entire extension — Counterevidence: K is not a finite or polar set.

P1 — Supergeometric approximation on sparse degrees does not force entire extension — Counterevidence: Failure is not caused by poles outside the allowed set.
P2 — Unit Green function requires local pole multiplicity, not total degree — Counterevidence: Discrepancy is inside grey faces and does not depend on the zero-extension convention.
P2 — Unit Green function requires local pole multiplicity, not total degree — Counterevidence: A single-pole map has m_p=d, explaining why that case does not expose this issue.
P3 — Repeated zeros supply fewer interpolation conditions than counted — Counterevidence: Same poles and same orders hold, so different pole divisors do not explain nonuniqueness.

proposition.claim:
A rational lemniscate is \(L_r(c)=\{|r|=c\}\), \(c>0\). The paper uses ambient sphere homeomorphisms of uniformly small spherical displacement, not merely setwise proximity, in Theorem A. Theorem B permits a compact \(K\subset\widehat{\mathbb C}\), exactly one prescribed point in every complementary component, and a function holomorphic on a neighborhood of \(K\). It asserts degree-\(\le n\) rational approximants with poles in that prescribed set and error \(A/B^n\), for some \(A,B>1\).

For nonextendible f, some D>1 forces error>C/D^n for every sufficiently large n and every C>0/admissible sequence.
